dua.en: Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise.

positions.title: Opening Takbir
positions.meaning: Raising both hands to the ears saying Allahu Akbar.

positions.title: Bowing
positions.meaning: Bowing with back flat, hands on knees.

dua.en: Glory to my Lord, the Most Great.

positions.title: Prostration
positions.meaning: Forehead, nose, palms, knees, and toes on the ground.

dua.en: Glory to my Lord, the Most High.

positions.title: Testimony
positions.meaning: Sitting with right index finger raised while reciting the testimony.

dua.en: All greetings, prayers, and good things belong to Allah.

positions.title: Salutation
positions.meaning: Turning the head right and then left to conclude the prayer.

dua.en: Peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah.

positions.title: Standing Folded
positions.meaning: Standing with hands folded on the chest, right over left.

dua.translit: Allahumma ba'id bayni wa bayna khatayaya
dua.en: O Allah, distance me from my sins.

prayers.name: Fajr
prayers.note: Pre-dawn prayer — the most beloved to Allah. Two rak'ah before sunrise.

prayers.name: Dhuhr
prayers.note: Midday prayer — four rak'ah after the sun passes its zenith.

prayers.name: Asr
prayers.note: Afternoon prayer — four rak'ah. Guard this prayer especially.

prayers.name: Maghrib
prayers.note: Sunset prayer — three rak'ah just after the sun sets.

prayers.name: Isha
prayers.note: Night prayer — four rak'ah. Completes the five daily prayers.

learn.title: Why we pray
learn.body:
Prayer is the second pillar of Islam and the first act we will be asked about on the Day of Judgement. It is a direct connection between the servant and their Lord — a moment of stillness in a busy day, a time to reset the heart. The Prophet ﷺ said: "The covenant between us and them is the prayer; whoever abandons it has disbelieved." (Tirmidhi).

Prayer is not a burden — it is a mercy. It washes away sins as a river washes away dirt. Five times a day, we return to our Creator and remember why we exist.

learn.title: Conditions of prayer
learn.body:
Before praying, ensure these conditions are met:

1. Purity — Wudu (or Ghusl if required) and clean body, clothes, and place.
2. Time — each prayer has its own valid time window.
3. Qibla — face the direction of the Kaaba in Makkah.
4. Covering — men cover from navel to knee; women cover the whole body except face and hands.
5. Intention — the niyyah in the heart to pray that specific prayer.

Missing any of these invalidates the prayer.

learn.title: What breaks prayer
learn.body:
A prayer is invalidated by: speaking deliberately, laughing aloud, eating or drinking, turning the chest away from the Qibla, excessive movement without need, or losing purity (e.g. passing wind, bleeding, urinating).

If this happens, the prayer must be repeated after renewing Wudu. Small movements — scratching, adjusting clothing — do not break the prayer.
